title: PDMC: Generating Feasible Algorithmic Recourse via Perturbation Data Manifold Constraint

problem.claim: Algorithmic recourse aims to provide actionable insight into how modifying input features can change algorithmic decisions.

gap.claim: Existing studies use differing feasibility notions and complex optimization constraints that rely on strong assumptions and expert knowledge, limiting practical and broad applicability.

contributions.claim: The paper provides a theoretical clarification of feasibility challenges by modeling adherence to the perturbation data manifold.
The paper introduces Perturbation Data Manifold Constraint (PDMC), an optimization-constraint framework for generating feasible algorithmic recourses.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on simulated and real clinical data evaluating the rationale and effectiveness of PDMC.

narrative_sequence.summary: Algorithmic recourse is introduced to help individuals understand and adjust outcomes of algorithmic decisions.
Prior approaches may depend on restrictive feasibility notions, complex constraints, strong assumptions, and expert knowledge.
The paper models typical feasibility challenges through adherence to the perturbation data manifold and designs optimization constraints accordingly.
The resulting method is called the Perturbation Data Manifold Constraint (PDMC).
Experiments on simulated and real clinical data are reported as validating PDMC's rationale and effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Modeling feasibility through adherence to a perturbation data manifold is presented as a way to address practical recourse constraints.

interpretation.claim: A data-manifold constraint may encode typical feasible perturbations without relying solely on manually specified expert constraints.

application.claim: When designing actionable recourse methods, consider data-supported manifold constraints as a candidate mechanism for representing feasibility.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish applicability beyond the reported simulated and real clinical settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the perturbation-manifold construction or optimization formulation.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experiment conditions.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical clarification in detail.
